articles.title: WBHRC directs DG Prisons to submit a report on the poor living conditions at Midnapore Correctional Home
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The West Bengal Human Rights Commission (WBHRC) has sought a detailed report from the Director General (DG) of Correctional Services on the poor living conditions and lack of infrastructure for inmates at Midnapore Central Correctional Home.

The development came in the wake of a formal complaint by general secretary of the Association for Protection of Democratic Rights (APDR), Altaf Ahmed, with the State’s Human Rights Commission recently. Over the last few months, a delegation from the organisation repeatedly visited the Midnapore jail and spoke with a section of inmates, families visiting prisoners and those who had been released or granted bail.

Based on their visits, APDR members also submitted a memorandum to the jail superintendent. However, as the situation failed to improve, APDR approached the State Human Rights Commission with a complaint last August and also submitted a memorandum to the Inspector General (Prisons).

“The West Bengal Human Rights Commission has sought a report from the Director General of Prisons (DG Prisons) regarding the pathetic state of the Midnapore Central Correctional Home, specifically concerning the quality and quantity of food and the mismanagement of medical treatment,” said APDR vice president said in a statement.

Apart from the quantity and quality of food and medical facilities, a major issue at this jail during the monsoon is rainwater leaking heavily through the roofs of certain wards, causing immense suffering to the inmates. Repeatedly bringing this to the attention of authorities yielded no results, it added. After receiving the complaint from APDR, the WBHRC directed the DG to take immediate cognisance of the matter and submit the report within seven weeks.

Earlier this year, an outbreak of Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) was reported at Jalpaiguri Central Correctional Home, with over 90 infections and seven of infected inmates losing their lives. As per the 2023 Prison Statistics of India, a report published by the Ministry of Home Affairs, district prisons in West Bengal have reported an occupancy rate of 158%. The prisons in the State are also burdened by a high number of inmates who are foreign nationals, particularly those from Bangladesh.

articles.title: M.P. police officers caught on CCTV threatening to plant ganja in couple’s bag; inspector faces inquiry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: An inspector of Madhya Pradesh Police, a head constable and two other personnel have been suspended after a CCTV footage showed some officers threatening a couple of putting marijuana in their bags to make a fake case during a search at a private hotel in Seoni district, officers said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).

Jabalpur Zone Inspector General (IG) of Police Pramod Verma said that the role of Seoni district Additional Superintendent of Police Deepak Mishra, who is heard making the threat, and City SP Chanchlesh Markam, who is also seen in the viral video, is being probed in a departmental inquiry.
Mr. Verma said that the initial probe has established the presence of all six officers.

“DIG Chhindwara (Rakesh Kumar Singh) is conducting a probe and he has been asked to submit an interim report by today evening and a final report by tomorrow (Thursday, November 19, 2026) evening,” he said.
Mr. Verma also said that he has spoken to the hotel owner, who has accused the cops of demanding ₹50,000 a month, and taken his allegations into cognisance.
The suspended officers are Inspector Satish Tiwari, Kotwali police station in-charge; a head constable and two other personnel — driver and gunman of the Additional SP.

The CCTV footage, dated November 13, shows the officers questioning a young couple staying at the hotel. In the video, Mr. Mishra is heard asking police personnel to “put ganja (marijuana) in their bag” after the woman requests the officers not to inform her parents.
“We won’t call your parents but then we’ll keep ganja your bag. Put ganja in the bag,” Mr. Mishra is heard saying.

Following the incident, Kotwali police station in-charge Satish Tiwari was attached to the police line. However, no action has been taken so far against Mr. Mishra and City SP Chanchlesh Markam, who is also seen in the footage.

Speaking to The Hindu , Chhindwara Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Rajesh Kumar Singh, who is conducting the inquiry, said any action against the senior officers would depend on the findings of the investigation.
“We have initiated the probe and are gathering all the facts. The inspector has been line-attached,” he said.
Meanwhile, another CCTV footage, dated October 9, purportedly shows Mr. Tiwari and a constable scolding the hotel staff.

articles.title: KUDA allocates ₹1.91 crore for drinking water supply in Kalaburagi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: In an initiative to address the drinking water crisis, the Kalaburagi Urban Development Authority (KUDA) has approved an allocation of ₹1.91 crore from water cess funds to strengthen drinking water infrastructure in Kalaburagi city and its surrounding areas. The decision was taken at a KUDA meeting chaired by its Chairman Mazhar Alam Khan on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Under the allocation, 65% of the funds, amounting to ₹1.24 crore, will be released to the Kalaburagi City Corporation, while the remaining 35%, amounting to ₹67 lakh, will go to the Rural Drinking Water and Sanitation Department.
The allocation is aimed at addressing drinking water requirements in the city and neighbouring areas and strengthening the existing water supply infrastructure.

The meeting was attended by Kalaburagi North MLA Kaneez Fatima, Kalaburagi South MLA Allamprabhu Patil, Kalaburagi Rural MLA Basavaraj Mattimood, MLCs Tippannappa Kammakanur, B.G. Patil and Jagadev Guttedar, KUDA Commissioner and officials of various departments.

articles.title: DISA India, part of a Danish industrial tech group, Norican, expands its manufacturing facility in Tumakuru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: DISA India Limited, part of Norican, an industrial technology group headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, on Monday (November 16, 2026) announced a significant expansion of its manufacturing footprint in Tumakuru by adding over 8,000 sq. metres of additional space alongside the existing facility.

The new state-of-the-art facility is a key part of Norican’s continued investment and expansion in India and it will manufacture equipment and solutions across all four of Norican’s technology brands: DISA, Wheelabrator, Simpson and StrikoWestofen, serving both domestic and international markets, as per information shared by the company.

By bringing these capabilities together at Tumakuru, Norican was aiming to strengthen local manufacturing capabilities, enhance operational efficiencies and improve responsiveness to customers, it said, adding that, the expansion would also reinforce India’s contribution to Norican’s global supply network, while creating opportunities for further growth and development.

Speaking on the occasion, Ulla Hartvig Tonnesen, President & CEO of Norican, said, “India is a strategically important market and a key growth region for Norican. The inauguration of this expanded manufacturing facility reinforces our long-term commitment to India and reflects our confidence in the country’s manufacturing potential.”

Through continued investments in technology, innovation, manufacturing excellence and sustainable growth, the company plans to further strengthen its ability to support customers in India and globally. “This investment also creates exciting opportunities for our employees and the wider manufacturing ecosystem,’’ Mr. Tonnesen added.
The inauguration ceremony was attended Peter Winther Schmidt, Consul General, Head of Trade & Innovation, Embassy of Denmark in India.

Lokesh Saxena, Managing Director & CEO, DISA India Limited, said the expanded facility demonstrated the company’s commitment to investing in India and strengthening Tumakuru’s position as an integral part of Norican’s global manufacturing network. “The additional capacity and enhanced capabilities will provide us with greater flexibility to respond to evolving customer requirements, support our growth ambitions and serve markets across the world,’’ he said.
The greenfield expansion marked a significant milestone in Norican’s growth journey in India and reinforced the country’s growing importance within its global manufacturing network, the firm said.

DISA has been serving customers in India with advanced foundry and surface treatment solutions for the last four decades. Over the years, its Tumakuru operations have evolved into an important global manufacturing and engineering hub, serving customers across the country and also supporting Norican’s worldwide operations, the firm elaborated.

articles.title: About 50 students of Keralam school hospitalised after suspected pollution from tar-mixing unit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 50 students of Auxilium ISC School at Kottiyam in Kollam district of Keralam were rushed to a nearby private hospital on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) afternoon after experiencing acute health distress, including severe breathing difficulties, nausea, and vomiting. The sudden medical emergency sparked panic among parents and school authorities, prompting an immediate evacuation of the affected classrooms.

Local residents and parents have strongly alleged that toxic fumes emanating from a tar-mixing unit located in close proximity to the school campus triggered the incident. According to them, thick smoke began drifting into the school premises shortly after the facility resumed operations earlier in the day.

This is not the first time the industrial unit has been linked to health hazards in the area. In a similar incident previously, more than 10 students from the same school were hospitalised with identical symptoms. Following public outcry and protests from parents at the time, the panchayat had issued a formal stop memo, forcing the unit to suspend its operations.

However, tensions flared again on Wednesday morning when the tar-mixing plant reopened after securing a favourable court order. Within hours of the machinery starting up, dozens of children began falling ill.
“We warned the authorities that restarting this unit would put our children’s lives at risk. How can a court order override the basic right of these children to breathe clean air?” a parent asked.

Echoing the sentiment, a local resident demanded permanent closure of the facility. “The panchayat issued a stop memo earlier because the pollution was unbearable. After they restarted the plant this morning, ambulances were rushing our children to the hospital. We will not allow this unit to function here anymore,” he said.
Hospital authorities confirmed that the admitted students are currently under close medical observation and their condition is reported to be stable.

articles.title: Season’s first ground frost recorded in Nilgiris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The first seasonal ground frost was recorded in the Nilgiris on the intervening night of Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and Wednesday (November 18), as temperatures between 5°C and 6°C were recorded in the higher elevations of the district.

While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025. However, the delay in the onset of ground frost led to colder weather in the early part of that year, with many places, especially Thalakundha, becoming tourist hotspots as the area was blanketed by ground frost.
While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025 | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

According to officials, ground frost was seen early Wednesday morning in the low-lying parts of Ooty town surrounding Ooty lake, as well as in Thalakundha, Khandal, and a few other areas. Temperature gauges recorded lows of anywhere between 5°C and 6°C.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon, which occurs when ground temperatures fall below freezing, causing ice crystals to form from condensed water vapour and creating the illusion of snow carpeting open expanses, particularly grasslands.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

The ground-frost season also has ecological implications, with the phenomenon helping to curtail the spread of invasive species into the upper Nilgiris, as many species of invasive flora are unable to tolerate the extreme cold that native and endemic species have evolved to withstand and thrive in.

articles.title: Rising prices reflect government’s economic mismanagement: Congress
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Congress on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) accused the Union government of fuelling inflation through its “economic mismanagement and anti-people policies” and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi remained preoccupied with politics rather than addressing the economic distress faced by households and businesses.

Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh cited a survey which found that, for 61% of families across the country, monthly household expenditure had risen by more than 20% over the past year. While 74% of respondents were cutting back on non-essential spending, 50% had reduced purchases of essential goods, he said.
Citing the survey, Mr. Ramesh said prices of ghee and edible oils had risen by 75%, vegetables by 73%, cereals by 71%, milk and dairy products by 65%, and pulses by 62%.

He also claimed that 200 garment factories had shut down in Noida over the past year, citing the impact of U.S. tariffs, high input costs, and government apathy. He said the closures reflected the wider distress in the textile industry.

“People’s plates are shrinking, and factories are being locked down. Yet, the Prime Minister’s only concern remains politics,” he said on X, accusing the government of failing to acknowledge people’s hardships or offer relief.

fullParagraphs: The story so far: Amid escalating geopolitical tensions, a boom in the AI sector, and valuation concerns, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have been exiting the Indian market for the last two years. However, in a change of course, FPIs have returned to India, and pumped the Indian markets with all-time high inflows of ₹89,856 crore so far in November.

The recent slowdown in AI stocks and concerns about their growth prospects have brought investors seeking a safer bet back to India. The boom in global AI and tech stocks over the last two years prompted investors to move too heavily into tech-heavy countries like the U.S., South Korea, and Taiwan.

fullParagraphs: There is no serious doubt that poverty in India has fallen sharply over the past decade. However, researchers and policymakers cannot agree on how many are still poor. Depending on the estimate, the share ranges from about 5% to more than 26%. Take the recent World Bank report. At its international line of $3 a day (2021 PPP), 2.6% of Indians were poor in 2022-23. Raise the line to $4.20, the bank’s benchmark for lower middle-income countries, and the figure jumps to around 16.1%. Same country, same year. Only the yardstick changed. A low level of extreme poverty does not necessarily mean poverty is not still a major issue. Where you draw the line decides how much economic insecurity you see.

India’s own figures tell a similar convoluted story. For example, SBI Research (2025) takes the Tendulkar line of 2009, adjusts it for inflation, and gets poverty of 7.2% in rural India and 4.6% in urban India for 2022-23. Rangarajan and Dev (2014), using an inflation-adjusted version of the Rangarajan Committee line, arrive at 10.8%. Further, Sethu, Surya and Ruthu (2024), who rebuild the Rangarajan method from the latest consumption survey, report 26.4%. Most of that gap boils down to the lines themselves: SBI’s Tendulkar-based lines use, after adjusting for inflation, about ₹1,632 a month per person in rural areas and ₹1,944 in urban areas. In contrast, Sethu et al. use much higher thresholds of ₹2,515 and ₹3,639. And the outcomes are obvious: Higher lines, higher poverty. Method matters too. One camp takes an old line and adjusts it for inflation. The other reconstructs the line from spending patterns in the new survey. Both have limitations, and they are answering different questions.

articles.title: Export duty on diesel hiked ₹2.5/litre, ATF ₹1.5/litre, petrol remains nil
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The government late Monday (November 16, 2026) hiked the export duty on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹2.5 per litre and ₹1.5 per litre, whilst keeping the levy on export of petrol unchanged at nil.
Duty rates on petrol and diesel meant for domestic consumption remain unchanged.
The hike in diesel levy assumes added significance as India looks to further up their exports of the vehicular fuel to Europe amid a global supply crunch.
In the upcoming fortnight, diesel exports would draw a levy of ₹14 per litre compared to ₹11.5 per litre mandated for the previous fortnight.
ATF exports would draw a levy of ₹12.5 per litre against ₹11 per litre.

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Wholesale inflation in India surged to 12.3% in October 2026, the second consecutive month of double-digit inflation, official data released on Monday (November 16, 2026) showed. Fuel prices continue to be the main reason for the price rise, with the crude petroleum and natural gas sectors seeing inflation of more than 70%.

The new series of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry has data that goes back to only April 2024 and so a historical analysis for a longer duration is not possible. However, the data shows that inflation in October was the highest since at least then.
This data follows the release of Consumer Price Index data last week that showed that even retail inflation had climbed above the Reserve Bank of India’s upper comfort mark of 6% in October 2026.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, it is only a matter of time before wholesale inflation translates into a further increase in the prices consumers pay.

“It has been seen that manufactured goods in particular have witnessed an increase of 9.5%, with high inflation rates in textiles, tobacco products, chemicals, rubber products, metals and electrical equipment,” Mr. Sabnavis pointed out. “This will pressurise companies into increasing their product prices at some point of time.”
“This passthrough will get reflected in the core part of the CPI in the coming months depending on the actions of industry,” he added.

Further, as Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive argues, the high WPI inflation makes a rate hike by the RBI in December a near certainty, which would have a further dampening effect on the economy.

“The sharp rise in WPI inflation to 12.39% in October 2026 reinforces the inflationary concerns already reflected in elevated retail inflation readings,” Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive said. “As a result, a rate hike by the RBI in the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting [in December] now looks almost certain.”

“Higher interest rates may impact lending activity, investments, and consumption, while sentiment across the financial sector could remain under pressure,” Ms. Pandya added. “With geopolitical tensions resurfacing in the Russia-Ukraine region, risks to inflation and economic growth have become even more pronounced.”

Within the WPI, food inflation climbed to 8.3% in October 2026, the highest in 22 months. The overall fuel and power category saw inflation jump to nearly 33% in the same month, compared to about 26% in September 2026. These high levels were, however, also a result of a low base, since this segment of the WPI was in contraction for large parts of 2025.
Similarly, the crude petroleum and natural gas segment saw inflation climb to 70.8% in October 2026 from 57.3% in September. This was compared to a 7.2% contraction in prices in October of last year.

articles.title: U.S. proposes tougher rules for employment-based green cards, longer hiring process
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The U.S. has proposed stricter rules for employment-based green cards for foreign workers to ensure that Americans get priority in recruitment for jobs ranging from physical therapists and nurses to highly skilled professionals.

The Department of Labour on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) proposed a new rule to modernise the labour market test under the Programme Electronic Review Management (PERM) immigrant visa process, the first major revision of the rules in 20 years.
Under the proposed changes, employers would be prohibited from tailoring job opportunities to foreign workers.
The proposed rule would require employers to level the playing field when recruiting workers by using the same channels and methods when advertising jobs.
The proposal seeks to replace traditional print advertisements with online recruitment through employer websites, job portals, social media platforms, job fairs and campus recruitment.

It would also extend the minimum period for advertising vacancies from the existing 30 days to 90 calendar days and require employers to demonstrate that they had made genuine efforts to recruit qualified American workers.
“This proposed rule change will ensure American workers are first in line for high-skilled, high-paying job opportunities over foreign labour,” Secretary of Labour Keith Sonderling said.
The department also proposed to eliminate the administrative exemption that allowed employers to bypass the statutory labour market test for certain occupations.

Under the revised framework, employers recruiting for physical therapists, nurses, and positions requiring exceptional ability in the sciences or arts would have to consider qualified American applicants.

The proposal also seeks to strengthen safeguards for American workers who have been laid off. Employers would be required to continue considering qualified laid-off workers throughout the labour certification and immigrant petition processes.
Comment | The U.S.’s immigration blocks as a self-defeating path
It would bar certain employers who have laid off American workers within the preceding two years from seeking permanent labour certification for the same or similar positions.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank chair backs CEO after reports expose past lapses; Trump calls tax leak ‘illegal’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Deutsche Bank’s chairman backed ​his CEO Christian Sewing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) after a huge cache of leaked internal records renewed scrutiny ⁠of the German lender’s past dealings with clients including Russian oligarchs, U.S. President Donald Trump and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

The reports, compiled by a consortium of international journalists and published by outlets including Der Spiegel , the Financial Times , the New York Times and Le ‌Monde , examined Deutsche Bank’s dealings with Mr. Trump, Epstein and Russian oligarchs, including its pursuit of business in Russia before the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
Deutsche Bank, whose shares fell by as much as 6%, ‌said the matters in the various reports “date back many years”, and that the bank had since strengthened its ‌controls.
Christian Sewing, Chief Executive Officer of Deutsche Bank | Photo Credit: Reuters

“During ⁠my tenure, I haven’t seen a single decision from Christian Sewing that I was not comfortable ⁠with,” Deutsche Bank Chairman Alexander Wynaendts said in an emailed statement. Mr. Sewing has led Germany’s biggest lender since 2018.

The Financial Times reported that Deutsche Bank had inadvertently sent a Trump tax document to another client’s accountant in 2017 when the President was a Deutsche Bank client during his first ​term in office.
Asked in Manila about the ‌error, Mr. Trump said the bank should not have disclosed it. “They shouldn’t have done it. It’s illegal for them to do it,” Mr. Trump said.
Deutsche Bank declined to comment on Mr. Trump’s reaction.

The leaks also showed that Deutsche Bank was ambitious in pursuing business in Russia, including with high-profile oligarchs, right up to the invasion ‌of Ukraine in February 2022, even as some of the bank’s managers voiced concerns over the risks, according ​to the publications.

German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil called on authorities to investigate “and take the necessary action”. Deutsche Bank, he said, needs to explain “with complete transparency” how it has fixed failures and will ⁠prevent new ones.

A member of the European Parliament called on Mr. Sewing to appear before the body to answer questions about the bank’s business practices and control mechanisms. The European Central Bank and the Bank of England’s regulatory arm declined to comment.
The ‌6% share drop was the biggest since April 2025. Shares recouped some losses to trade 3.8% lower by early afternoon.

articles.title: Why did the U.S. lose its measles elimination status? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The story so far: After 26 years of holding on to its measles elimination status, the United States lost this distinction. On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organisation (PAHO) revoked the United States’ measles elimination status. This was after over 5400 cases of measles were reported in the U.S. in 2026.

This is the highest annual total since 1989-91, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention(CDC). As per data put out by the Unicef, 96% of cases are in unvaccinated people or those with unknown vaccination status. Children under five account for 18% of cases and those aged 5-19 for 40%.

fullParagraphs: Bahrain and Kuwait said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) that they had repelled air attacks launched against them following U.S. strikes on an Iranian island, as Gulf nations face retaliatory bombardment in the Middle East war.
The conflict — which began with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February — has spilled over to Gulf states that host U.S. military facilities.

The Iranian army said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) its drones "targeted Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms belonging to the terrorist US military at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait," in a statement carried by state television IRIB.
Kuwait's military said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) its air defences were "responding to hostile drone threats", urging its public to follow security and safety advice.
While Bahrain said its air defences intercepted attacks from Iran early on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), a day after Tehran's Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a base used by Washington.

The United States and Iran are in a standoff over the vital Strait of Hormuz, with the U.S. military working to escort ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Tehran's attempts to close the waterway.
Iran's official IRNA news agency cited a regional official as saying the United States had hit Qeshm Island in the Hormuz strait without causing serious damage.

U.S. fighter jets "used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island", an American official told AFP on condition of anonymity, adding that the strike was in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets".
Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) it had intercepted a cruise missile launched by the Iran-backed group toward the Riyadh area.
Explosions boomed across Bahrain's capital on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) as a mobile phone alert warned residents to seek safety.

Bahrain's armed forces said they "confronted, intercepted and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today... before they could achieve their objectives", while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a U.S.-operated radar system.

"Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said.

articles.title: Israeli Parliament elects new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu's opponents
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The Israeli Parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday (November 18, 2026), a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu. Eisenkot's bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu's most contentious policies following Kahana's election.

He was approved as speaker with 66 votes in the 120-member chamber, backed by the Jewish-led opposition parties and by the Arab-led parties. The candidate backed by Netanyahu's bloc, Ofir Katz, received 52 votes following a stormy debate that stretched over seven hours.
"The appointment of Matan Kahana as Knesset speaker is a worthy democratic move that reflects the absolute majority in favour of change," Mr. Eisenkot said ahead of the vote.

The vote took place weeks after October 27 parliamentary elections in which Netanyahu and his allies lost their parliamentary majority. Mr. Eisenkot was subsequently given the task by Israel's president to try to form a new coalition government.

Mr. Eisenkot has up to five more weeks to secure enough alliances to form a coalition. As negotiations continue on the sidelines, his bloc, along with unaffiliated Arab-led parties, can use their majority in the newly-sworn in Knesset to advance their legislative agenda. They introduced several bills last week, including to set term limits on the role of prime minister, to form a government-led inquiry into the Hamas-led Oct 7, 2023, attacks and to reverse laws to limit the powers of the judiciary.
Mr. Kahana gives the opposition bloc a major legislative advantage, according to Assaf Shapira with the Israel Democracy Institute, a Jerusalem think tank.
"It's important because there is not much time, because the speaker of the Knesset can make the legislative process much, much faster or much slower," Shapira said.
Mr. Kahana replaced Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally, as speaker.

Mr. Eisenkot and his allies are under pressure to swiftly advance their legislative priorities in the weeks ahead. Currently a member of Eisenkot's Yashar party, Roy Folkman, heads the temporary committee that decides much of the Knesset's work until a government is formed.
If Mr. Eisenkot fails to form a government, the Israeli President could give Netanyahu an opportunity to do so. That would likely give Netanyahu's Likud party control of the committee.

Even though Netanyahu's opponents would still hold a majority, they would "feel that their momentum has gone," Shapira said, and there would be a "real danger that some of the legislation will be delayed."

fullParagraphs: The story so far: After 26 years of holding on to its measles elimination status, the United States lost this distinction. On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organisation (PAHO) revoked the United States’ measles elimination status. This was after over 5400 cases of measles were reported in the U.S. in 2026.

This is the highest annual total since 1989-91, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention(CDC). As per data put out by the Unicef, 96% of cases are in unvaccinated people or those with unknown vaccination status. Children under five account for 18% of cases and those aged 5-19 for 40%.

articles.title: Gilead signs generic licensing deals for experimental Ebola drug
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Gilead Sciences said on Monday it had signed royalty-free deals with three generic drugmakers to make its experimental Ebola prevention drug available in 127 mainly low- and lower-middle-income countries if it succeeds in trials and wins regulatory approvals.

The deals with Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories, Eva Pharma and Ferozsons Laboratories cover obeldesivir, and include all African countries reporting cases in the current Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak. Obeldesivir has shown activity against several Ebola-related viruses in preclinical studies but is not approved for any use in any country.
A late-stage trial is testing the drug in people at high risk after exposure. The deals are intended to line up manufacturing and supply before trial results and regulatory filings.

Gilead is also expanding remdesivir licences to cover Ebola-related diseases if trial results are positive and regulators approve the drug. The company has donated more than 38,000 remdesivir vials to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and Kenya, including more than 2,000 recently sent to Kenya for investigational treatment and post-exposure prevention.
Remdesivir is not approved to treat or prevent Ebola Bundibugyo disease, and its clinical effectiveness has not been established.

articles.title: CCMB study points to new way of tackling fungal infections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad, have identified a promising new strategy to combat fungal infections by preventing disease-causing fungi from becoming invasive, rather than killing them outright.

Most current antifungal drugs work by destroying fungal cells. However, fungi can gradually develop resistance to these medicines, making infections increasingly difficult to treat. A team led by Sriram Varahan at CCMB studied ‘Candida albicans’, a fungus commonly found on human skin and in the body. While generally harmless, it can cause serious infections when it enters the bloodstream or internal organs.

The researchers focused on ‘morphogenesis’, in which the fungus changes from a round-cell form into long, filament-like structures, a transformation allowing the pathogen to evade the body’s immune defences and spread more effectively within tissues.

Earlier studies had shown that glycolysis, the process through which cells metabolise sugar, plays a key role in controlling this shape change. Building on these findings, the team screened a library of small molecules that target glycolysis and identified two compounds capable of blocking the transformation.

Although the fungus continued to grow, it remained in its harmless rounded form suggesting that the compounds could serve as “anti-infective” agents that reduce the fungus’ ability to cause disease without necessarily eliminating it.

The study also identified pyruvate kinase, an enzyme involved in sugar metabolism, as a crucial regulator of fungal morphogenesis. Researchers further found that one of the compounds reduced biofilm formation, a protective layer that helps fungi resist treatment. The compound also increased the effectiveness of widely used antifungal drugs such as fluconazole and amphotericin B.

In a mouse model of systemic Candida infection, treatment with the lead compound significantly improved survival rates, highlighting its potential for future therapeutic development. “Our findings suggest that fungal disease-associated behaviour can be targeted without necessarily stopping fungal growth,” said Dhrumi Shah, first author of the study. “We need further studies to evaluate the compounds effectiveness and safety but by blocking the fungus from becoming invasive, they could complement existing treatments,” said Sriram Varahan.

The findings, published in ACS Infectious Diseases , emerged from a collaboration between CSIR-CCMB and the BRIC-Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, said a press release on Tuesday.

articles.title: Scrap the Shillong Peak Ropeway Project, say civil society groups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: For nearly a fortnight, women from the Laban Pyllun area and other parts of Shillong have been peacefully protesting the ₹151-crore Shillong Peak Ropeway Project proposed near the Lum Shillong water catchment area. The project, which hopes to augment local tourism, could disrupt local water supply to the community as its many springs and streams will be undermined, the protestors claim.

The women, under the aegis of the Joint Action Committee Against the Shillong Ropeway Project and for the Protection of the Lum Shyllong Catchment (JAC) are demanding that the Meghalaya government scrap the project that could imperil the ecology of the area.

articles.title: Voyager 1, one light-day away from earth today, is a marvel of science
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Today, the Voyager 1 spacecraft will be one light-day away from the earth. This means a signal travelling at the speed of light will take one full day to go from the earth to Voyager 1, and signals from the spacecraft will similarly take one day to reach receivers on the earth.

This is a tremendous distance — almost 26 billion kilometres. Since February 17, 1998, Voyager 1 has been the farthest any space mission has been from us. And it keeps going at 61,000 km/hr. But even at such breathtaking speed, Voyager 1 is still barely out of the solar system. Each star’s gravitational and magnetic fields extend out for billions of kilometres around them, bending the destinies of multiple worlds to their stellar will.

articles.title: Elusive peace: On Kashmir terror attack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days. On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Though the security agencies need to be focused on Pakistan-backed terrorism, it should not come at the cost of re-inflicting psychological scars within Kashmir, which could turn into a powder keg if left unattended. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.

articles.title: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

articles.title: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

articles.title: Clear the path: On SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

articles.title: A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

articles.title: Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.title: WBHRC directs DG Prisons to submit a report on the poor living conditions at Midnapore Correctional Home
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The West Bengal Human Rights Commission (WBHRC) has sought a detailed report from the Director General (DG) of Correctional Services on the poor living conditions and lack of infrastructure for inmates at Midnapore Central Correctional Home.

The development came in the wake of a formal complaint by general secretary of the Association for Protection of Democratic Rights (APDR), Altaf Ahmed, with the State’s Human Rights Commission recently. Over the last few months, a delegation from the organisation repeatedly visited the Midnapore jail and spoke with a section of inmates, families visiting prisoners and those who had been released or granted bail.

Based on their visits, APDR members also submitted a memorandum to the jail superintendent. However, as the situation failed to improve, APDR approached the State Human Rights Commission with a complaint last August and also submitted a memorandum to the Inspector General (Prisons).

“The West Bengal Human Rights Commission has sought a report from the Director General of Prisons (DG Prisons) regarding the pathetic state of the Midnapore Central Correctional Home, specifically concerning the quality and quantity of food and the mismanagement of medical treatment,” said APDR vice president said in a statement.

Apart from the quantity and quality of food and medical facilities, a major issue at this jail during the monsoon is rainwater leaking heavily through the roofs of certain wards, causing immense suffering to the inmates. Repeatedly bringing this to the attention of authorities yielded no results, it added. After receiving the complaint from APDR, the WBHRC directed the DG to take immediate cognisance of the matter and submit the report within seven weeks.

Earlier this year, an outbreak of Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) was reported at Jalpaiguri Central Correctional Home, with over 90 infections and seven of infected inmates losing their lives. As per the 2023 Prison Statistics of India, a report published by the Ministry of Home Affairs, district prisons in West Bengal have reported an occupancy rate of 158%. The prisons in the State are also burdened by a high number of inmates who are foreign nationals, particularly those from Bangladesh.

articles.title: M.P. police officers caught on CCTV threatening to plant ganja in couple’s bag; inspector faces inquiry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: An inspector of Madhya Pradesh Police, a head constable and two other personnel have been suspended after a CCTV footage showed some officers threatening a couple of putting marijuana in their bags to make a fake case during a search at a private hotel in Seoni district, officers said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).

Jabalpur Zone Inspector General (IG) of Police Pramod Verma said that the role of Seoni district Additional Superintendent of Police Deepak Mishra, who is heard making the threat, and City SP Chanchlesh Markam, who is also seen in the viral video, is being probed in a departmental inquiry.
Mr. Verma said that the initial probe has established the presence of all six officers.

“DIG Chhindwara (Rakesh Kumar Singh) is conducting a probe and he has been asked to submit an interim report by today evening and a final report by tomorrow (Thursday, November 19, 2026) evening,” he said.
Mr. Verma also said that he has spoken to the hotel owner, who has accused the cops of demanding ₹50,000 a month, and taken his allegations into cognisance.
The suspended officers are Inspector Satish Tiwari, Kotwali police station in-charge; a head constable and two other personnel — driver and gunman of the Additional SP.

The CCTV footage, dated November 13, shows the officers questioning a young couple staying at the hotel. In the video, Mr. Mishra is heard asking police personnel to “put ganja (marijuana) in their bag” after the woman requests the officers not to inform her parents.
“We won’t call your parents but then we’ll keep ganja your bag. Put ganja in the bag,” Mr. Mishra is heard saying.

Following the incident, Kotwali police station in-charge Satish Tiwari was attached to the police line. However, no action has been taken so far against Mr. Mishra and City SP Chanchlesh Markam, who is also seen in the footage.

Speaking to The Hindu , Chhindwara Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Rajesh Kumar Singh, who is conducting the inquiry, said any action against the senior officers would depend on the findings of the investigation.
“We have initiated the probe and are gathering all the facts. The inspector has been line-attached,” he said.
Meanwhile, another CCTV footage, dated October 9, purportedly shows Mr. Tiwari and a constable scolding the hotel staff.

articles.title: DISA India, part of a Danish industrial tech group, Norican, expands its manufacturing facility in Tumakuru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: DISA India Limited, part of Norican, an industrial technology group headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, on Monday (November 16, 2026) announced a significant expansion of its manufacturing footprint in Tumakuru by adding over 8,000 sq. metres of additional space alongside the existing facility.

The new state-of-the-art facility is a key part of Norican’s continued investment and expansion in India and it will manufacture equipment and solutions across all four of Norican’s technology brands: DISA, Wheelabrator, Simpson and StrikoWestofen, serving both domestic and international markets, as per information shared by the company.

By bringing these capabilities together at Tumakuru, Norican was aiming to strengthen local manufacturing capabilities, enhance operational efficiencies and improve responsiveness to customers, it said, adding that, the expansion would also reinforce India’s contribution to Norican’s global supply network, while creating opportunities for further growth and development.

Speaking on the occasion, Ulla Hartvig Tonnesen, President & CEO of Norican, said, “India is a strategically important market and a key growth region for Norican. The inauguration of this expanded manufacturing facility reinforces our long-term commitment to India and reflects our confidence in the country’s manufacturing potential.”

Through continued investments in technology, innovation, manufacturing excellence and sustainable growth, the company plans to further strengthen its ability to support customers in India and globally. “This investment also creates exciting opportunities for our employees and the wider manufacturing ecosystem,’’ Mr. Tonnesen added.
The inauguration ceremony was attended Peter Winther Schmidt, Consul General, Head of Trade & Innovation, Embassy of Denmark in India.

Lokesh Saxena, Managing Director & CEO, DISA India Limited, said the expanded facility demonstrated the company’s commitment to investing in India and strengthening Tumakuru’s position as an integral part of Norican’s global manufacturing network. “The additional capacity and enhanced capabilities will provide us with greater flexibility to respond to evolving customer requirements, support our growth ambitions and serve markets across the world,’’ he said.
The greenfield expansion marked a significant milestone in Norican’s growth journey in India and reinforced the country’s growing importance within its global manufacturing network, the firm said.

DISA has been serving customers in India with advanced foundry and surface treatment solutions for the last four decades. Over the years, its Tumakuru operations have evolved into an important global manufacturing and engineering hub, serving customers across the country and also supporting Norican’s worldwide operations, the firm elaborated.

articles.title: About 50 students of Keralam school hospitalised after suspected pollution from tar-mixing unit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 50 students of Auxilium ISC School at Kottiyam in Kollam district of Keralam were rushed to a nearby private hospital on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) afternoon after experiencing acute health distress, including severe breathing difficulties, nausea, and vomiting. The sudden medical emergency sparked panic among parents and school authorities, prompting an immediate evacuation of the affected classrooms.

Local residents and parents have strongly alleged that toxic fumes emanating from a tar-mixing unit located in close proximity to the school campus triggered the incident. According to them, thick smoke began drifting into the school premises shortly after the facility resumed operations earlier in the day.

This is not the first time the industrial unit has been linked to health hazards in the area. In a similar incident previously, more than 10 students from the same school were hospitalised with identical symptoms. Following public outcry and protests from parents at the time, the panchayat had issued a formal stop memo, forcing the unit to suspend its operations.

However, tensions flared again on Wednesday morning when the tar-mixing plant reopened after securing a favourable court order. Within hours of the machinery starting up, dozens of children began falling ill.
“We warned the authorities that restarting this unit would put our children’s lives at risk. How can a court order override the basic right of these children to breathe clean air?” a parent asked.

Echoing the sentiment, a local resident demanded permanent closure of the facility. “The panchayat issued a stop memo earlier because the pollution was unbearable. After they restarted the plant this morning, ambulances were rushing our children to the hospital. We will not allow this unit to function here anymore,” he said.
Hospital authorities confirmed that the admitted students are currently under close medical observation and their condition is reported to be stable.

articles.title: Season’s first ground frost recorded in Nilgiris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The first seasonal ground frost was recorded in the Nilgiris on the intervening night of Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and Wednesday (November 18), as temperatures between 5°C and 6°C were recorded in the higher elevations of the district.

While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025. However, the delay in the onset of ground frost led to colder weather in the early part of that year, with many places, especially Thalakundha, becoming tourist hotspots as the area was blanketed by ground frost.
While frost usually sets in in late November or early December, the season was extremely delayed in 2025 | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

According to officials, ground frost was seen early Wednesday morning in the low-lying parts of Ooty town surrounding Ooty lake, as well as in Thalakundha, Khandal, and a few other areas. Temperature gauges recorded lows of anywhere between 5°C and 6°C.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon, which occurs when ground temperatures fall below freezing, causing ice crystals to form from condensed water vapour and creating the illusion of snow carpeting open expanses, particularly grasslands.

Over the last few years, pictures of the district’s annual ground frost have led to an increase in tourism footfall in the district, with visitors keen to witness this weather phenomenon | Photo Credit: M. Sathyamoorthy

The ground-frost season also has ecological implications, with the phenomenon helping to curtail the spread of invasive species into the upper Nilgiris, as many species of invasive flora are unable to tolerate the extreme cold that native and endemic species have evolved to withstand and thrive in.

articles.title: A poverty line that falls short
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: There is no serious doubt that poverty in India has fallen sharply over the past decade. However, researchers and policymakers cannot agree on how many are still poor. Depending on the estimate, the share ranges from about 5% to more than 26%. Take the recent World Bank report. At its international line of $3 a day (2021 PPP), 2.6% of Indians were poor in 2022-23. Raise the line to $4.20, the bank’s benchmark for lower middle-income countries, and the figure jumps to around 16.1%. Same country, same year. Only the yardstick changed. A low level of extreme poverty does not necessarily mean poverty is not still a major issue. Where you draw the line decides how much economic insecurity you see.

India’s own figures tell a similar convoluted story. For example, SBI Research (2025) takes the Tendulkar line of 2009, adjusts it for inflation, and gets poverty of 7.2% in rural India and 4.6% in urban India for 2022-23. Rangarajan and Dev (2014), using an inflation-adjusted version of the Rangarajan Committee line, arrive at 10.8%. Further, Sethu, Surya and Ruthu (2024), who rebuild the Rangarajan method from the latest consumption survey, report 26.4%. Most of that gap boils down to the lines themselves: SBI’s Tendulkar-based lines use, after adjusting for inflation, about ₹1,632 a month per person in rural areas and ₹1,944 in urban areas. In contrast, Sethu et al. use much higher thresholds of ₹2,515 and ₹3,639. And the outcomes are obvious: Higher lines, higher poverty. Method matters too. One camp takes an old line and adjusts it for inflation. The other reconstructs the line from spending patterns in the new survey. Both have limitations, and they are answering different questions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Both have limitations, and they are answering different questions.

articles.title: Export duty on diesel hiked ₹2.5/litre, ATF ₹1.5/litre, petrol remains nil
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The government late Monday (November 16, 2026) hiked the export duty on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹2.5 per litre and ₹1.5 per litre, whilst keeping the levy on export of petrol unchanged at nil.
Duty rates on petrol and diesel meant for domestic consumption remain unchanged.
The hike in diesel levy assumes added significance as India looks to further up their exports of the vehicular fuel to Europe amid a global supply crunch.
In the upcoming fortnight, diesel exports would draw a levy of ₹14 per litre compared to ₹11.5 per litre mandated for the previous fortnight.
ATF exports would draw a levy of ₹12.5 per litre against ₹11 per litre.

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Wholesale inflation in India surged to 12.3% in October 2026, the second consecutive month of double-digit inflation, official data released on Monday (November 16, 2026) showed. Fuel prices continue to be the main reason for the price rise, with the crude petroleum and natural gas sectors seeing inflation of more than 70%.

The new series of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry has data that goes back to only April 2024 and so a historical analysis for a longer duration is not possible. However, the data shows that inflation in October was the highest since at least then.
This data follows the release of Consumer Price Index data last week that showed that even retail inflation had climbed above the Reserve Bank of India’s upper comfort mark of 6% in October 2026.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, it is only a matter of time before wholesale inflation translates into a further increase in the prices consumers pay.

“It has been seen that manufactured goods in particular have witnessed an increase of 9.5%, with high inflation rates in textiles, tobacco products, chemicals, rubber products, metals and electrical equipment,” Mr. Sabnavis pointed out. “This will pressurise companies into increasing their product prices at some point of time.”
“This passthrough will get reflected in the core part of the CPI in the coming months depending on the actions of industry,” he added.

Further, as Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive argues, the high WPI inflation makes a rate hike by the RBI in December a near certainty, which would have a further dampening effect on the economy.

“The sharp rise in WPI inflation to 12.39% in October 2026 reinforces the inflationary concerns already reflected in elevated retail inflation readings,” Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive said. “As a result, a rate hike by the RBI in the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting [in December] now looks almost certain.”

“Higher interest rates may impact lending activity, investments, and consumption, while sentiment across the financial sector could remain under pressure,” Ms. Pandya added. “With geopolitical tensions resurfacing in the Russia-Ukraine region, risks to inflation and economic growth have become even more pronounced.”

Within the WPI, food inflation climbed to 8.3% in October 2026, the highest in 22 months. The overall fuel and power category saw inflation jump to nearly 33% in the same month, compared to about 26% in September 2026. These high levels were, however, also a result of a low base, since this segment of the WPI was in contraction for large parts of 2025.
Similarly, the crude petroleum and natural gas segment saw inflation climb to 70.8% in October 2026 from 57.3% in September. This was compared to a 7.2% contraction in prices in October of last year.

articles.title: U.S. proposes tougher rules for employment-based green cards, longer hiring process
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The U.S. has proposed stricter rules for employment-based green cards for foreign workers to ensure that Americans get priority in recruitment for jobs ranging from physical therapists and nurses to highly skilled professionals.

The Department of Labour on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) proposed a new rule to modernise the labour market test under the Programme Electronic Review Management (PERM) immigrant visa process, the first major revision of the rules in 20 years.
Under the proposed changes, employers would be prohibited from tailoring job opportunities to foreign workers.
The proposed rule would require employers to level the playing field when recruiting workers by using the same channels and methods when advertising jobs.
The proposal seeks to replace traditional print advertisements with online recruitment through employer websites, job portals, social media platforms, job fairs and campus recruitment.

It would also extend the minimum period for advertising vacancies from the existing 30 days to 90 calendar days and require employers to demonstrate that they had made genuine efforts to recruit qualified American workers.
“This proposed rule change will ensure American workers are first in line for high-skilled, high-paying job opportunities over foreign labour,” Secretary of Labour Keith Sonderling said.
The department also proposed to eliminate the administrative exemption that allowed employers to bypass the statutory labour market test for certain occupations.

Under the revised framework, employers recruiting for physical therapists, nurses, and positions requiring exceptional ability in the sciences or arts would have to consider qualified American applicants.

The proposal also seeks to strengthen safeguards for American workers who have been laid off. Employers would be required to continue considering qualified laid-off workers throughout the labour certification and immigrant petition processes.
Comment | The U.S.’s immigration blocks as a self-defeating path
It would bar certain employers who have laid off American workers within the preceding two years from seeking permanent labour certification for the same or similar positions.

Christian Sewing, Chief Executive Officer of Deutsche Bank | Photo Credit: Reuters
